paper.title: MOSAIC: An Omni-Modal Benchmark for Long-Term Memory and Cross-Modal Reasoning in Conversational Agents

latest_version.version_label: OpenReview anonymous ACL submission reviewed on 2026-08-30

evidence.figure_or_table: Figure 1; benchmark overview and question-type tables
evidence.paraphrase: MOSAIC contains 923 questions embedded in persona-grounded conversations spanning 11-24 sessions and multiple months. Six question types test factual recall, knowledge updates, temporal reasoning, cross-modal selection and bridging, and refusal when the history does not support an answer.

evidence.section: Appendix D (modality statistics and modality-gap construction)
evidence.paraphrase: The required evidence spans text, image, audio, and video, with images supplying the largest share of required facts (911 of 1,860, 49.0%). The construction includes image detail and spatial gaps, video event-order and state-transition gaps, and audio prosody gaps that prevent replacement by redundant text.

Native omni-modal, caption-to-text, and omni-to-text systems are evaluated with retrieval and memory baselines. The best reported system reaches 64.9% accuracy; the stated 91.3% ceiling is a corrected answerability estimate rather than human QA accuracy, and the human audit is deliberately stratified toward difficult probe failures.

adjudication_notes: Benchmark-only record: the paper introduces a dataset and evaluation framework, not a distinct persistent-memory architecture.
primary_modality set to image because images provide the largest share of load-bearing required evidence; video, audio, and text remain operative secondary modalities.
The exact OpenReview posting date is left blank rather than inferred from the search index's rounded '3 months ago' label; the forum and PDF were reviewed on 2026-08-30.
The paper states that the benchmark and evaluation framework are released, but no independently accessible code or data repository was located during review.
